summary: AI coding assistants sometimes invent names of software packages that do not exist. A researcher registered one such invented name as a harmless test and it was downloaded thousands of times, showing how attackers could plant malware this way.
technical_summary: Large language models hallucinate plausible but non-existent package dependencies when generating code. Because the same fake names recur, an attacker can register them on public registries so that developers following AI suggestions install malicious code, an attack termed slopsquatting.
